description: Propose the whole setup of a site in one plan: the kind of site it is, the collections and singles to create (with fields and the records to import), the block types its pages are made of, the page map, the site's forms, the files you will change and the packages you will install. Model what the owner manages, not the copy of each page, by what the owner will do with it: what the site shows in several places is one record, linked — a fact lives on the object it describes, so a product's sizes are fields of the product, shown wherever the site shows them, never sentences of a guide; what the owner adds and removes is a record of a collection (same-shaped rows of one page alone may be a repeatable group); the sections of a content page (a hero, a list of features, a text, a gallery, a call to action) are blocks of a components field, so the owner adds, reorders and removes them; what exists once is a single (the site's settings, a page's fixed parts). Only the site's interface (a cart, a search) stays in code. The page map (pages) lists every page of the site — one of each kind for a route that serves many — with its blocks top to bottom and where each block's content lives. Mapled reads each page from the deployed site and refuses a plan that leaves out a page the site's menus link to, or that holds less than 90 % of what a page shows (its words, numbers and pictures), quoting what is missing; read_site_pages shows a page as Mapled reads it. Name the kind in site.kind and give collections that carry it a role. A shop needs products (price, stock, every photo in one gallery field, a 3D model file when the site shows one, variants), orders and customers — orders and customers operational with accessClass server, written by the site's server on each paid checkout; Mapled refuses a shop plan without them and says what to add. Every form of the site (contact, newsletter, returns) goes under forms. The plan waits for the project's builder to approve it on a trusted Mapled screen — nothing changes until then. Use this for the initial integration instead of creating collections one by one. Write the summary, notes, display names and help texts in English (records stay in the site's language). Name everything for the person who edits it: a page that becomes a single takes the page's name ("Shipping"), and every collection starts with a short text field (Title, Name) that each record fills with the name people know it by — the page's h1 or title, the item's name. A plan whose records would show as "Untitled" is refused. Record keys are the field keys: the lowercase, hyphenated display name ("Show badge" → "show-badge"). Relation fields name their target collection (one of this plan by its display name, or an existing one by key); give a record a "$ref" (a short name) and other records of the plan link to it by that name, in a relation field or in a block's relation sub-field — links to existing collections use record ids. Group fields carry their sub-fields; their values are objects keyed by the sub-field keys. Images and files are content too: model every picture the site shows (product photos, covers, logos, avatars) as an image field, never a text field holding a path, and import it — in a record, an image or file field takes the file's path in the site's repository or its public address, written { "$media": "public/products/hoodie.jpg" }. Nothing is uploaded while the plan waits; once it is approved, upload the plan's media (apply_setup_plan says how) and the records point at the files in Mapled's Media, where the person can replace them. Returns the run id and reviewUrl: give the user the link — they approve on that screen, not in this conversation — then, without ending your turn, poll get_setup_run until the status is "approved", call apply_setup_plan and carry on without asking.

accessClass.description: public (default): the site reads it with the delivery key. server: only the site's server reads it, with the server key — anything private.

components.description: For type components only: a page's sections as blocks the owner adds, reorders and removes. In records the value is the list of blocks in page order, each { "_type": "<type key>", …values by sub-field key }.

allowed.description: The block types a value may hold: names of this plan's componentTypes, or keys of the project's (get_schema's componentTypes).

max.description: The most blocks a value holds (100 by default).

min.description: The fewest blocks a value holds (0 by default).

computed.description: For type computed only: { expression } — a formula over the record's other fields that Mapled evaluates when a record is read or published (read-only for editors and agents; the site reads the value like any field of the result type, filters and sorts included; writes ignore it). Field keys as written (price, unit-cost — put spaces around a minus to subtract: price - cost); up to two links through relations: author.name, author.company.name, and lists over many-relations for aggregates: sum(items.price), count(tags), join(tags.name, ", "), sum(items.product.price); or one link back — the records of another collection whose relation points at this record, written @collection.relation[.field], always a list, oldest first: count(@posts.author), sum(@order-items.order.total), max(@posts.author.published-on) — and one more link on from them: sum(@order-items.order.product.price). A path goes through at most one list (a many-relation, or the records that link back), so items.tags.name is refused. Numbers: + - * / %, round(x, digits), floor, ceil, abs, min, max, sum, avg, count, fixed(x, digits) → text. Text: & joins (empty counts as ""), concat, upper, lower, trim, length, left(s, n), right(s, n), replace(s, from, to), contains(s, part), slug(s), text(x), number(s). Logic: = != < <= > >=, and, or, not, if(cond, a, b), coalesce(a, b), empty(x). Dates: year, month, day, date(datetime), daysBetween(a, b), addDays(d, n), created() — when the record was added (a datetime). Literals: 12, 2.5, "text", true, false, null. today() and now() — the day and the moment the value was computed: a publish bakes them into the release, and Mapled recomputes the current release once a day (after midnight UTC), sending the publish webhook again — so daysBetween(today(), due) counts down, but not by the minute; a pinned release keeps its values. Sensitive fields and relations, groups, JSON and location can't be read. The result type (number, text, boolean, date, datetime) follows from the formula. In a plan the formula may read fields of this plan (this collection, or another one through a relation); one that doesn't check is skipped with a warning when the plan is applied.

group.description: For type group only. In records the value is an object keyed by the sub-field keys (lowercase, hyphenated names) — or an array of such objects when repeatable.

sensitive.description: Masked in lists and history and never delivered to the site — this sub-field's values stay with the editors.

repeatable.description: true (default): a list of items; false: one nested object

options.description: For type enum only: the values a record may hold, in display order.

relation.description: For type relation only. In records the value is the $ref of a record in this plan (an array of $refs for many), or record ids when the target collection already exists.

cardinality.description: one (default): the record links to one record; many: to a list of them, in the order given.

onDelete.description: What a delete of a linked record does: restrict — it can't be deleted while linked; nullify — the links are cleared. Default: restrict when the field is required, nullify otherwise.

target.description: The display name of a collection in this plan, or the key of a collection the project already has (see get_schema). Singles can't be targets.

sensitive.description: Masked in lists and history and never delivered to the site — for data editors keep but the site must not show. A group takes it on its sub-fields instead.

mode.description: editorial (default): drafts that people publish. operational: Live data the site's server writes and reads at once — orders, customers, bookings (Pro and Max; on Free only a shop's orders and customers).

records.description: Records keyed by field key. Add "$ref": "<short name>" to a record so relation fields of other records in the plan can link to it; $ref is not stored.

role.description: What the collection is for beyond page copy. A shop's products, orders, customers and inventory (SKU and stock, taken off by each order's items), a blog's posts, take their role.

componentTypes.description: Block types the plan adds — the sections pages are made of (Hero, Text, Feature, Gallery, Call to action): a name and the sub-fields a block holds (a group's sub-field types; none sensitive, no components inside). What repeats inside a section — a pricing block's tiers, an FAQ's questions — is a sub-field of type group with its own sub-fields in group.fields, and a block holds it as a list of objects. Records a section picks — featured products, related posts — are a sub-field of type relation naming their collection (of this plan by name, or the project's by key), and a block links them by $ref or record ids. Its key is the lowercase, hyphenated name; a block names it in _type. Created when the plan is applied.

group.description: For type group only: the sub-fields of each of its items (simple types, no group inside) and up to how many items it holds; a block holds it as a list of objects keyed by those sub-fields' keys.

relation.description: For type relation only: the records a block picks (featured products, related posts). In a record's block the value is the $ref of a record in this plan (an array of $refs for many), or record ids when the collection already exists.

cardinality.description: one (default): a block holds one linked record; many: a list of them (their order is kept).

onDelete.description: What a delete of a linked record does: restrict — the linked record can't be deleted while a block links to it; nullify — the links are cleared. Default: restrict when the sub-field is required, nullify otherwise.

target.description: The display name of a collection in this plan, or the key of a collection the project already has (see get_schema) — not a single, nor one of the site's signed-in users.

forms.description: Every form of the site that should reach the owner — contact, newsletter, returns, wholesale. Created when the plan is applied; the site posts to /v1/delivery/forms/{key} with the delivery key.

pages.description: The page map: every page of the site with its blocks top to bottom and where each block's content lives. Mapled reads each page from the deployed site and refuses the plan when it leaves out a page the site's menus link to, or when less than 90 % of what a page shows is in it.

code.description: Instead of collection: why the block stays in the site's code — the site's interface (a cart, a search, a calculator), never its content.

collection.description: The collection or single its content lives in: one of this plan by display name, or the project's by key.

fields.description: The fields of that collection the block shows, by display name.

name.description: The block as the page shows it, top to bottom: "Hero", "Size table", "Sections".

text.description: What the site's code writes in this block, word for word — a unit, a column label, the words of an interface: left out of the page's measure and shown to the person.

name.description: What people call the page: "Fit guide".

path.description: The page's path as a visitor opens it: "/", "/fit-guide", "/blog/first-post" — for a route that serves many pages, one of them.

route.description: The route in the code that serves it, when it serves many: "/blog/[slug]".

site.description: The kind of site. Always send it.

evidence.description: What in the code told you, in English, one short line each: "Cart and checkout in app/cart", "Stripe in package.json". The owner sees it on the plan screen.

kind.description: What the code shows the site is: shop (cart, checkout, a payment provider), blog, docs, landing, portfolio or other.

url.description: The public address the site is deployed at now (https://…): Mapled reads the page map's pages there. Leave it out when the site isn't deployed yet — verify_setup reads them once it is.

name: propose_setup_plan
